title: Who am I? Two number riddles
description: Two riddles give clues about a mystery number. Listing the multiples that fit the factor clue and testing the digit clue gives each number, and a check puts them back against every clue.
teaching_notes: One idea: a factor clue means the mystery number is a multiple of that factor, so list the multiples and test the other clue. Watch for students who test numbers one by one without a list.

source: Figure it Out box 2, Q2, p.111
video_script.why: The child lists the multiples that fit the factor clue and tests the digit clue on each, so only one number is left.
video_script.substitution: A number with a given factor is a multiple of it, so list the multiples below the limit and test the other clue.
video_script.anchor: two riddles about a mystery number, with clues about its factors and its digits
video_script.payoff_line: The numbers are thirty five and forty five

final_answer.spoken: the numbers are thirty five and forty five

never_show: 35 as the answer to riddle two
maths_rules: a: multiples of 7 below 40 are 7, 14, 21, 28, 35; digit sums 7, 5, 3, 10, 8; sum 8 gives 35
b: numbers with factors 3 and 5 are multiples of 15; below 100: 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90
video_script.design: One idea: list the multiples of the factor clue, then test the other clue. Same method as the book example: factors and multiples go together.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about two riddles about a mystery number.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Riddle one says the number is less than forty, and seven is one of its factors.
<bookmark mark='digits'/>The digits of that number add up to eight.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Riddle two says the number is less than one hundred, and three and five are factors of it.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>One digit is one more than the other. Who am I in each riddle?

narration: <bookmark mark='list'/>Step one, riddle one. The multiples of seven below forty are seven, fourteen, twenty one, twenty eight and thirty five.
<bookmark mark='sums'/>Their digits add up to seven, five, three, ten and eight.
<bookmark mark='pick'/>Only the last one has digits that add up to eight.

beats.on_screen: Step 2 (b): multiples of 15 below 100: 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90; the digits of 45 differ by 1

marks.fifteen: the multiples of 15 below 100 are written
marks.gaps: the gap between the digits is written under 15 and 30
marks.pick: 45 glows and the other gaps are written

narration: <bookmark mark='fifteen'/>Step two, riddle two. The numbers that three and five both reach are the multiples of fifteen.
<bookmark mark='gaps'/>The digits of fifteen differ by four, and the digits of thirty differ by three.
<bookmark mark='pick'/>The digits of forty five differ by one. The others differ by six, two and nine.

beats.on_screen: Check: 35 = 7 x 5 and 3 + 5 = 8; 45 = 3 x 15 = 5 x 9, and 5 is 1 more than 4

marks.b: 45 = 3 x 15, 45 = 5 x 9 and 5 = 4 + 1 are written and all get a tick

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step three, put them back. Thirty five is seven times five, so seven is a factor, and three plus five is eight.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Forty five is three times fifteen and five times nine, and five is one more than four.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The numbers are thirty five and forty five.
